shows.name: Coltrane Day
shows.description:
NTS presents a special all-day broadcast dedicated to one of the most influential and acclaimed figures in the history of jazz and 20th century music: John Coltrane.
Across 12 hours of radio, we're enlisting the help of admirers and collaborators of Coltrane - We explore his musical beginnings, influences, and notable eras of his prolific composing and performing life. Featuring interviews and explorations by noted Coltrane experts, admirers, and NTS residents, including music journalist Ben Ratliff and Coltrane's jazz contemporary Ron Carter.

episodes.name: In Focus: Cecil Taylor
episodes.description:
Soon after he first emerged in the mid-’50s, pianist Cecil Taylor was the most advanced improviser in jazz; five decades later he is still the most radical. Although in his early days he used some standards as vehicles for improvisation, since the early ’60s Taylor has stuck exclusively to originals. To simplify describing his style, one could say that Taylor’s intense atonal percussive approach involves playing the piano as if it were a set of drums. He generally emphasizes dense clusters of sound played with remarkable technique and endurance, often during marathon performances. Suffice it to say that Cecil Taylor’s music is not for everyone." - Blue Note
Created by Claire Rousay

episodes.name: NTS Guide to: Indian Classical Influence on Jazz
episodes.description: In the mid-1950s musicians such as Yusuf Lateef and John Coltrane started to use instruments, structure and patterns based on traditional Indian music.  Artists sought to expand the boundaries of jazz by incorporating the modal structures, improvisational depth, and spiritual ethos of Indian music. Listen to two hours of Jazz inspired by Indian Classical.
